headlines.title: Oil prices jump over 4% as Trump rejects Iranian proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
headlines.summary: This is the tape-mover of the morning — a 4% crude spike touches everything from airlines and truckers to refiners and the long bond. With Brent already north of $104 and the Strait still choked, every day this drags on is another inflation print waiting to happen, and the Fed's October decision just got a lot more complicated.

headlines.title: Nvidia makes a statement with historic $150 billion buyback announcement
headlines.summary: A $150 billion buyback is not a rounding error — that's a management team putting its money where its mouth is on the AI cycle, and it'll put a floor under NVDA shares when the rest of the tape is getting hit by oil and yield fears. Expect the whole semiconductor complex to catch a bid on the open as the Street reprices the confidence signal.

headlines.title: Trump 'very seriously' considering diesel export ban as global supply crunch worsens
headlines.summary: If this export ban lands, refiners like Valero and Marathon get squeezed on margins while trucking and logistics costs rip higher across the whole economy — Goldman's already penciling in 30 cents a gallon at the pump. It's a policy wildcard that hits industrials, consumer staples, and inflation expectations all at once, and the Street hates uncertainty more than bad news.
